topic.title: File Comparison Tool
topic.shortdesc: Use the file comparison tool to compare the current document with the latest repository version or with another file.

body.p: includes a file comparison tool that shows differences between the current document and either its latest version from the repository or another document in a side-by-side interface.
The comparison tool can show differences between XML, Markdown, and plain text documents.

To access the tool, select one of the following actions in the More drop-down menu:
Compare with Latest version from repository - Opens the file comparison/merge tool with the current file displayed in the left pane and the latest version from the repository displayed in the right pane. If the file is not read-only and you are not in a Concurrent Editing session, the documents open in the Merge tool, and the file in the left pane can be edited and changes can be copied or merged.If you are using a Git file repository integration (GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, Azure DevOps, or Git), this action automatically performs a three-way comparison between the current document, its latest version from the repository, and the original base revision.
Compare with Another file (this submenu is replaced by the Compare with another file action if auto-save is enabled) - Opens a file browsing dialog box where you can choose a file to compare with the current file.
After you select a file and click Choose, the file comparison tool opens with the current file displayed in the left pane and the other file displayed in the right pane. If the file is not read-only and you are not in a Concurrent Editing session, the documents open in the Merge tool, and the file in the left pane can be edited and changes can be copied or merged.

The tool visually compares the two files, displaying the documents in each pane similarly to how they appear in the Web Author visual editor. Detected differences are grouped into highlighted blocks in each pane. Darker highlighting within the blocks identifies specific changes. Dynamic lines connect each block of differences between the two panes.
The markers on the right-side vertical stripe help you quickly locate differences. Click a marker to navigate to a specific difference.

The toolbar at the top also includes navigation buttons, a Tags Display Mode drop-down button that lets you select how many tags to display for XML files, and a Toggle Text Mode button to show differences in the XML source (text mode).The default tags display mode is Full Tags With Attributes so that XML structural differences, such as element name changes or attribute changes, are more visible. You can switch to a less cluttered view by choosing the No Tags mode.

When showing differences in text mode, the toolbar contains a Toggle Ignore Whitespaces button that enables or disables whitespace ignoring. When whitespace is ignored, the application normalizes the content and trims leading and trailing whitespace before performing the comparison.

The comparison tool also shows differences made using the Change Tracking feature. Content that has an attached comment is highlighted in the same color used in the editor. To see the comment content, hover over it.
body.note: If you are using a version of that is integrated into another application (for example, a CMS), the file comparison tool may not be available by default.

section.title: Differences View
section.p: There is an expandable/collapsible Differences view on the far-right side. Its main purpose is to help you understand changes related to review comments. When an item is selected in the Differences view, the changed content is highlighted in the editor. If the change corresponds to a review comment, a pop-up box with the comment's conversation thread is displayed below the change in the document. The pop-up box also contains inline actions to reply to the comment or remove the thread. You can also hover over a difference that contains a review comment in the editor to see a pop-up of the comment. To navigate between items in the Differences view, you can use the mouse, the toolbar navigation buttons, or keyboard keys (arrow keys, Tab, Shift+Tab).

If the Oxygen AI Positron for Web Author plugin is installed, the header of the Differences view displays the following buttons:
Explain Differences - The AI assistant explains the differences for the entire document.
Explain Current Block of Differences - The AI assistant explains the differences in the current block of content.You can also ask the AI to explain differences or how to resolve conflicts directly in the chat input box in the AI Positron view.

section.title: Three-Way Comparisons
section.p: A three-way comparison compares two documents while also considering their common base version at the point where they diverged. This method helps identify conflicts between the two documents.

If you are using a Git file repository integration (GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, Azure DevOps, or Git), when comparing the current document to its latest version from the repository, it automatically does a three-way comparison between the current document that is open in the editor, its latest version from the repository, and the original base revision.

When you commit a file to a Git repository and there is a conflict, you are presented with the choice to Merge and Commit. This option allows you to visualize and resolve the conflict before committing.

In this type of comparison, the differences are highlighted in the following additional colors:
Pink - Identifies differences on both sides where conflicts are possible.
Gray - Identifies a node added on the left side (the current document).
Blue - Identifies a node added on the right side (the latest version from the repository).
Darker Shade - Identifies specific changes within the blocks.
